open: LcnLayers.SLOTS has no row for the tutorial, so boot logs 'canvas layers not in LcnLayers.SLOTS yet: LcnTutorial@80' on every launch and enforce() will not correct my layer. Adding {key: &"tutorial", layer: MODAL, owner: "P21 tutorial", names: ["LcnTutorial"]} is a one-line integrator change in game/core/ui_layers.gd — INTEGRATOR owns it.

LcnLayers.PENDING advertises the tutorial's hotkey as 'F1 help', but F1 is a readability lens ([P16] action map -> [P19]) and tests/boot/run_reachability.tscn asserts that. I took no key at all; the guide is mouse-only on real Buttons, like [P22]'s card. Either that PENDING row's hotkey text should change or the INTEGRATOR should allocate a key that nobody else has claimed.

The guide has no way to be brought back once skipped except LcnTutorialRoot.restart(), which nothing in the interface calls. A 'Show the guide' line belongs in [P24]'s settings screen; the method is public and takes no arguments.

user://tutorial.cfg is my own ConfigFile because game/core/settings.gd is [P24]-owned and read-only to other parts. If [P24] lands a save-game, tutorial progress should move into it so a loaded city resumes its lesson rather than resuming the course.

The suite drives the pipe runs with build place_line commands, not with a real click-and-drag through PlayController. The commands are the same ones the drag submits, but the drag itself is [P11]/integrator-owned and untested from here.

Not run: tools/check.sh in full (40+ min, and perf numbers are meaningless with four agents on this box). Under check.sh my suite runs headless and will therefore be recorded as a SKIP, not a pass, because of that one display-dependent check — same shape as tests/boot/run_reachability.tscn.
